name: Okta — Authentication Brute Force From Single IP
xql_query:
dataset = okta_sso_raw
| filter eventType contains "session.start" or eventType contains "authentication"
| alter outcome_result = arrayindex(regextract(outcome, "\"result\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0),
        ip = arrayindex(regextract(client, "\"ipAddress\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0),
        user_name = arrayindex(regextract(actor, "\"alternateId\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0)
| filter outcome_result = "FAILURE" and ip != null and user_name != null
| filter not (incidr(ip, "10.0.0.0/8") or incidr(ip, "172.16.0.0/12") or incidr(ip, "192.168.0.0/16"))
| bin _time span = 15m
| comp count() as fails by ip, user_name, _time
| filter fails >= 5
| fields user_name, ip
description: ≥5 Okta authentication FAILURE events from one source IP within 30 minutes — credential spraying / brute force.
alert_name: Okta — Authentication Brute Force From Single IP
alert_description:
What fired: ≥5 Okta authentication FAILURE events from one source IP within 30 minutes — credential spraying / brute force.

Why it matters: an actor is attempting to obtain or brute-force credentials. Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1110 - Brute Force (TA0006 - Credential Access).

Investigate:
  - Identify the targeted account(s) and the source IP, and check for a SUCCESSFUL authentication following the failures.
  - Determine whether the source is expected; look for MFA prompts, password resets, or new sessions from the same source.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (ip) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.
